correctness.rationale: Native 2m-coordinate facet-normal lengths are 1, sqrt(2), 2. The first-row and total-supply chains give rigorous independent radius upper bounds, and the explicit baseline center satisfies every margin inequality at their minimum. Equality saturation gives necessary and sufficient optimal-center parametrizations below, at, and above the crossover. The t=0 transformation into unit Pitman–Stanley coordinates has exact Euclidean scale sqrt(2)c in m-1 independent directions; the original vertex census follows from a two-chain order polytope. Exact Python rational enumeration and integration through m=12 plus 36 independent SciPy LP tests support but do not replace the all-m analytic proof. Full domain m>=1, real t>=0.

Neither the inspected primary geometry nor the indexed all-ones statement asserts the competing total-supply branch, sharp t threshold, all three center-locus regimes or the emergence of a parking-function polytope as the zero-source incenter set. Uninspected plausible adjacent full texts are disclosed as risks, not declared non-covering.
residual_risks: The complete text of the indexed all-ones staircase metric result could not be inspected; exact broader scope cannot be excluded from its summary alone. Its stated all-ones radius is explicitly prior.

Unindexed equivalent literature or a broader general Chebyshev-center theorem could cover the result; no priority guarantee is asserted.

value.rationale: A natural Euclidean Chebyshev-center problem in a newly studied grid polytope admits a complete all-dimensional/continuous-parameter solution with a sharp irrational critical supply, a 0-dimensional collapse between two positive-dimensional solution families, and an exact boundary incenter polytope with exponentially many vertices and Cayley-tree volume despite quadratically many original vertices. The geometry and the precise volume are motivated by optimizing centers, not by an arbitrary slice.
